note: 'the exile to Babylon' (Matt 1:17), named as a division twice.
'from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the exile to Babylon' (Matt 1:17). He is the only pivot the verse names twice, closing one block and opening the next.

Matthew begins the count at Abraham and does not say why. The promise of Gen 12:3 is what the corpus attaches to him, and Gal 3:16 reads it as running to Christ -- which is where Matthew's count ends. The graph makes this join; Matthew states only the endpoints.
'David added, The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion' (1Sam 17:37), ten verses before 'the battle is the Lord's'.
The Philistine is addressed throughout the speech and named at 1Sam 17:4 and 17:23; v47 says 'He will give all of you into our hands' without a name. Implied for that reason alone.
'it is not by sword or spear that the LORD saves' (1Sam 17:47). The word is used to say where the saving does not come from.
